paper.title_en: Quantum state texture from the average absolutes of density entries
paper.abstract_en: Quantum state texture is recently recognized as an important quantum resource in quantum information tasks. The only textureless state firstly proposed in $(Phys. Rev. Lett. 133, 260801 (2024))$ is $f_1=\ket{f_1}\bra{f_1}$, \textcolor{red}{where $\ket{f_1}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{d}}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\ket{i}$.} We take into account the modulus of the density matrix entries, and reasonably define the textureless states to be ones that all the modulus of the density matrix entries are equal. We present a quantifier of quantum state texture with respect to such non-convexity set of textureless states. As an application, we demonstrate in the transverse field Ising model that the texture of the subsystem of the ground state effectively characterize the quantum phase transitions, providing an alternative texture-based characterization of quantum criticality. We also provide the relationships among the quantum state texture, coherence and purity. Furthermore, we explore the quantum state texture based quantum speed limit in dissipative dynamical processes and derive the lower bound on the time required in texture variation for some dynamical processes.
